books.title: Software Engineering at Google: Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time

access.availability: Official complete HTML, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Raw chapter copies stayed outside the repository.
access.provenance: Official abseil/abseil.github.io mirror, master observed at e9e24835cb889fe25251cb9ec6d51b79233e358d on 2026-09-29.

findings.failure: Review becomes taste-driven redesign or an oversized approval queue.
findings.mechanism: Review correctness and comprehension against the intended change; automate mechanical checks and give extra reviewers distinct concerns.
findings.conditions: Use evidence and the repository convention; prefer bounded, coherent changes.
findings.counterexample: A small low-risk edit does not need every specialist.
findings.verification: Each finding identifies the affected behavior, supporting location, and required correction; track its resolution.

findings.trigger: Documentation is stale, conflicting, or hard to follow.
findings.failure: Readers cannot identify an authoritative instruction or its prerequisites.
findings.mechanism: Assign a canonical source and owner; keep audience-specific explanations separate and review instructions with an unfamiliar reader.
findings.conditions: Preserve operational rationale and discoverability while consolidating.
findings.counterexample: A tutorial and a complete reference can intentionally explain the same API differently.
findings.verification: Run relevant steps in a fresh context and check links, prerequisites, and audience comprehension.

findings.trigger: Cleanup breaks many tests without a requirement change.
findings.failure: Tests encode private call structure instead of the consumer contract.
findings.mechanism: Exercise the public boundary and assert meaningful outcomes; keep test inputs and expectations visible.
findings.conditions: Interaction assertions remain appropriate when interactions are the contract.
findings.counterexample: Deduplicating all test setup can conceal the scenario; copying production calculations can copy their bug.
findings.verification: A harmless internal change keeps tests green; a changed promised outcome makes a focused test fail.

findings.trigger: Unit tests cannot establish a deployment or dependency claim.
findings.failure: Doubles, packaging, configuration, load, or network behavior diverge from production.
findings.mechanism: Choose the smallest environment retaining the risky behavior; record real and substituted dependencies, data, action, oracle, and owner.
findings.conditions: Balance fidelity against isolation, cost, and failure risk.
findings.counterexample: A mock transaction cannot prove database isolation; a passing startup smoke check cannot prove business correctness.
findings.verification: Demonstrate the relevant defect, preserve diagnostic artifacts, and bound event-based waits; identify remaining fidelity gaps.

findings.trigger: An obsolete API or subsystem is proposed for removal.
findings.failure: Hidden users fail after an apparently safe deletion.
findings.mechanism: Inventory static and runtime consumers, migrate them, and prevent new dependencies during retirement.
findings.conditions: Removal needs a replacement or explicit withdrawal decision and a responsible owner.
findings.counterexample: Old code or a quiet telemetry interval alone does not prove obsolescence.
findings.verification: Verify migrated consumers and remaining dependency evidence; distinguish local refactoring from behavior-removing deprecation.

limitations: Google-specific numbers, ownership machinery, and production chaos practices are context, not universal mandates.
The book describes human peer review; fresh-agent review is a repository adaptation, not an empirically equivalent substitute.
The entire book was available; only the five listed chapters were read in depth.
Chapter 14 mathematical illustrations about fidelity are not adopted as measured reliability estimates.

findings.trigger: A test plan contains only habitual edge cases.
findings.failure: Generic empty/null inputs miss domain-specific boundaries.
findings.mechanism: Derive expected behavior and partitions from requirements before augmenting with familiar implementation edge cases.
findings.conditions: Scale formality to uncertainty and risk.
findings.counterexample: An empty-list case says nothing about a reservation limit or ownership transfer.
findings.verification: Every selected input distinguishes a stated requirement; the oracle is independently justified.

findings.trigger: A suite reaches a numerical coverage goal.
findings.failure: Executed branches are mistaken for effective assertions.
findings.mechanism: Use uncovered paths to question the requirement-derived suite and explain omissions.
findings.conditions: Coverage is a diagnostic, not a correctness certificate.
findings.counterexample: Tests can execute faulty behavior and still assert nothing relevant.
findings.verification: Introduce a representative fault and confirm an existing assertion detects it; explain untested risks.

findings.trigger: Mocks fail after changing a dependency.
findings.failure: Tests mix intended interactions with incidental collaborator details.
findings.mechanism: Name which observable interaction matters, then narrow coupling to that boundary.
findings.conditions: Preserve version rollback options when required by the integration.
findings.counterexample: External message emission can require an interaction assertion even when internal lookup calls do not.
findings.verification: A changed internal lookup preserves the test; a missing promised emission fails it.

limitations: Findings are supported by the linked author articles; they are not claims of reading the full book.
Book examples are Java-oriented; runtime-specific advice needs current language and dependency documentation.
No fixed coverage percentage, mandatory mock ban, or universal testing ratio is adopted.

books.title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code

access.availability: Official complete opening chapter available as a 45-page PDF (cover plus printed pages 1–44). Canonical full web edition requires registered book access.
access.search_scope: Author, publisher, Thoughtworks, and institutional/full-PDF searches; no authenticated open complete second edition located.

read_sections.scope: Complete chapter prose and successive code examples; printed pages 1–44; rendered printed page 38 to verify code-layout context.

findings.trigger: Structure obstructs a specific change or understanding.
findings.failure: A broad cleanup changes behavior or creates speculative abstraction.
findings.mechanism: Preserve observed results with self-checking tests and make small transformations with feedback.
findings.conditions: Choose structure for the next evidenced change; track cost as well as clarity.
findings.counterexample: Fewer lines is not automatically better; useful structure can increase code size.
findings.verification: Existing output expectations survive each step; review any changed expectation as a separate behavior decision.

limitations: The chapter demonstrates a method, not a mandate for inheritance, tiny functions, repeated calculation, or particular naming conventions.
Performance-sensitive paths still need representative measurement.
Full book was not read; public catalog entries are summaries, not full mechanics.

interpretation: Practice cards are original applications informed by each linked source. Counterexamples and verification checks are repository adaptations, not quotations or claims that the books prescribe these exact tests.
